description: Volodymyr Pavlov, a software engineer working on backend systems in Go, and writing about keeping them small.

descriptions.blog: Writing on Go backends: one store package, wrappers instead of layers, and a main you can read top to bottom.
descriptions.about: About Volodymyr Pavlov: a software engineer building backend systems in Go, and writing about keeping them small.
descriptions.privacy: How Volodymyr Pavlov handles visitor data: what the site and its host collect, and how long it is kept.
descriptions.contact: Send Volodymyr Pavlov a message about an article, a correction, or Go backends in general.

01-bitwise-in-go.description: Pack boolean flags and states into one integer with Go bit operations: set, clear and test bits, and keep structs small.

02-one-method-store-in-go.description: Build a Go data access layer around one generic interface with a single method, and keep it small without frameworks.

03-transactions-in-go.description: Wrap one-method Go stores in a SQL transaction so two tables change together or not at all, keeping the clean architecture.

04-bitwise-store-in-go.description: A clean Go architecture from one generic interface, typed bit flags and a stack of wrappers: flexible storage without a framework.

06-go-and-wasm.photoAlt: A cartoon beaver, bear and elephant watch a game of Go, a board with black and white stones.
06-go-and-wasm.description: Compile a Go game engine to WebAssembly, call it from a Web Worker with one exported function, and keep the hot loop allocation-free.

08-dj-go-on-ai-radio.description: How a Go radio keeps one shared stream cheap for every listener and lets a local language model act as its DJ without ever touching the audio path.

09-kubernetes-operator-for-an-s3-bucket-.description: A Go operator built with Operator SDK that keeps an S3 bucket equal to a custom resource, and never deletes a bucket it did not create.

10-ollama-go-auth.description: A Go auth service where fixed rules score each login and a small local model, served by Ollama, can only make the decision stricter. On the test data it changed no decision.
